contract: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) floats. Inputs are compositions {'formula': str, 'composition': {element: amount}}. Called once per official Matbench v0.1 fold (five calls, KFold(5, shuffle, random_state=18012019)), each in a fresh process that receives that fold's training inputs with targets and its held-out inputs without targets; info = {'task', 'input_type', 'target', 'unit', 'fold', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, RDKit and torch are importable; wall-clock limit 170 s per fold. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error in target units (minimize), the Matbench leaderboard metric
notes: Official Matbench v0.1 data (SHA-256 equal to matminer's recorded hashes) and folds. Reference check: the stored per-fold predictions of the published AMMExpress v2020 and RF-SCM/Magpie submissions rescored with this evaluator's folds and metric reproduce their leaderboard MAEs exactly (validation/chemistry-checks.json).
protocol_description: Locally implemented evaluator with recorded reference checks; consult the task-specific tests and evidence for their exact scope. This label alone does not establish reproduction of the paper's full experiment.
name: Matbench: steel yield strength from composition
description: Predict the yield strength (MPa) of 312 steels from their elemental composition alone. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error over Matbench's five official cross-validation folds.
benchmark: Matbench: steel yield strength from composition
paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

sources.locator: Xiong, Zhang and Shi (2020): machine learning of yield strength and other mechanical properties of steels from composition and processing.
Dunn et al. (2020): Matbench v0.1 tasks, nested cross-validation protocol and MAE metric.
matbench_v0.1_validation.json (official folds) and stored per-fold predictions of published submissions (pinned commit).
Per-task Matbench v0.1 leaderboard (mean MAE over the five folds).

limitations: All targets are public in the Matbench files and every sample is a test sample of one fold; candidates or settings tuned on these folds overfit, so treat scores as development scores.

Leaderboard entries were trained without this task's limits (170 s and at most 4 CPU threads per fold, CPU only), so leaderboard values are reference points rather than targets attainable under the same budget.
Only 312 steels, so fold MAEs vary by about 10 MPa; compositions omit processing history, which strongly affects strength; the Citrine source states no licence.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.
